_comment: task.testing.019: every place the Python implementation can race (threads, processes, SQLite, async tasks).
tests/test_concurrency_inventory.py scans the source for concurrency primitives and fails when a site
is not listed in some entry's sites, when a listed test does not exist, or when an entry is marked
unchecked but claims tests. 'unchecked' means no test exercises that order: it is NOT guaranteed.
Ledger methods run one SQLite transaction each (BEGIN IMMEDIATE); races are tested at that granularity.

entries.race: Two callers, threads or processes reserve one (principal, request_key) at the same time.
entries.guard: BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus UNIQUE(principal, request_key); the second caller reads the first operation.

entries.race: Two workers dispatch the same prepared operation.
entries.guard: State check and UPDATE ... WHERE state='prepared' in one transaction; leases fence workers.

entries.race: Two operations consume one host approval.
entries.guard: Approval consumption and dispatch commit together.

entries.race: A cancel request races dispatch and the result.
entries.guard: Before dispatch a cancel is terminal; after dispatch it is a flag and never an undo.

entries.race: A worker's lease expires while another process recovers expired work (ownership switch).
entries.guard: Owner token, session expiry and lease expiry are checked inside the finishing transaction; recovery quarantines to unknown.

entries.race: A request is cancelled while its SQLite work waits on a write lock in a worker thread.
entries.guard: Each transaction finishes before cancellation is acted on (abandon_on_cancel=False); a bounded thread limiter.

entries.race: A cancel intent must survive a process exit before SQLite records it.
entries.guard: The intent file and its directory are fsynced before cleanup; recovery replays it.

entries.race: A process is killed in the middle of a stream of transactions.
entries.guard: SQLite atomic commit; recovery marks interrupted dispatches unknown.

entries.race: Two executors call the external destination with one request key at the same time.
entries.guard: The ledger reservation decides; the second caller sees IN_PROGRESS. The result is stored before the ledger claims success.

entries.race: The sender delivers the same event twice at once, or a redelivery overlaps the first attempt.
entries.guard: Recording the delivery, applying it and marking it processed happen in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; the second delivery waits and then reads processed.

entries.race: A cancellation arrives while the request binds its new operation.
entries.guard: A lock serializes cancel and bind; only a newly reserved operation can bind.

entries.race: Concurrent model requests spend one call budget.
entries.guard: A lock reserves one call before the fixture runs.

entries.race: HTTP jobs share one execution slot; a cancel races the job's start.
entries.guard: One asyncio lock; a job checks for cancellation after taking the slot; only prepared jobs can be cancelled.

entries.race: Read-only calls wait for a bounded number of worker threads; a timed-out worker is still running.
entries.guard: A capacity limiter and a deadline that includes the queue wait.

entries.race: The host revokes a grant (an Event set by another thread) while a call is running.
entries.guard: The live grant is read again before each external request and at handoff.

entries.race: The stdio guard relays two directions in threads around a child process group.
entries.guard: Per-direction locks, deadlines on blocked peers, and process-group termination.

entries.race: A stalled reader of the diagnostics pipe while the server answers calls.
entries.guard: The diagnostics line is written only when select() reports stderr writable.

entries.race: An operator engages the kill switch (another process writes its file) while a call is between grant checks: after approval, or waiting out a rate limit.
entries.guard: Every grant check reads the switch, including the ledger's check inside the dispatch transaction and the check before a resend; once seen, a threading.Event keeps it engaged for every thread of the process.

entries.race: The MCP client cancels a recorded call at each checkpoint.
entries.guard: Cancellation before dispatch cancels; after dispatch it becomes unknown; after commit the result stays.

entries.race: The caller of an external change is cancelled while the request is in flight.
entries.guard: The worker thread is not abandoned; the change finishes and is recorded before cancellation is delivered.

entries.race: Orders inside one SQLite transaction.
entries.guard: SQLite's own serialization of BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions.
entries.reason: Interleavings are enumerated at transaction granularity only; SQLite's locking is relied on, not tested.

entries.race: The ledger on a network or multi-host file system.
entries.guard: None beyond SQLite; the documented scope is a single host.
entries.reason: Out of the documented scope (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, task.durable_operations.020); never run.

entries.race: The wall clock moves backwards, or processes on different hosts disagree on time.
entries.guard: None; lease and approval expiry use one host's ledger clock.
entries.reason: Out of the documented scope (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); expiry orders are tested only with a monotone test clock.

entries.race: Several HTTP server processes sharing job identifiers.
entries.guard: None; jobs live in one process's memory.
entries.reason: The local HTTP interface runs as one process; multi-worker deployments are not supported or tested.

entries.race: Free-threaded (no-GIL) CPython builds.
entries.guard: Locks are explicit, but nothing was run on such a build.
entries.reason: The pinned environment is CPython 3.13 with the GIL.

entries.race: Two processes reconcile the same unknown external operation at the same moment.
entries.guard: Each would record the same issue; the result store and the ledger are separate transactions.
entries.reason: Sequential reconciliation is tested; simultaneous reconciliation of one operation is not.

entries.race: More than two workers in one lease handover, or more steps than the enumerated actors.
entries.guard: The same per-transaction fencing.
entries.reason: Exhaustive orders cover two owners/recoverers and one clock step; longer schedules are sampled by the stress test only.
